key_insight: For medical imaging transfer, making global attention operate across features/channels instead of spatial layout can preserve from-scratch performance while substantially improving reuse of pretrained representations.
clinical_relevance: This could make foundation models more reliable and compute-efficient for medical image tasks where texture and feature correlations matter more than object geometry.
method: Built FAD-ViT, a vision transformer that strictly decouples spatial and feature axes.
Made feature-axis attention the primary global operator and kept the attention axis controlled.
Compared against standard and channel-attention baselines under matched tokenization, capacity, and training protocol.
evidence_signal: Across 23 classification, segmentation, and low-data tasks, feature-axis attention produced stronger transfer, with up to about 3x the transfer gain and consistent segmentation improvements under identical ImageNet pretraining.
watch_item: The approach was evaluated under controlled benchmarking, so real-world gains may depend on task type, scanner variability, and how faithfully the feature-axis design is implemented.
paper_title: Learning Features, Not Layouts: Feature-Axis Attention as a Transfer Prior for Medical Imaging
